summary: Evidence strength: direct for architecture conformance and requirements-to-code traceability, adjacent for broad prose drift. Studies show that intended/implemented differences can be computed and trace links can be captured, but no direct controlled study located validates one agent score spanning specifications, README files, roadmaps and decision records.

items.text: Murphy, Notkin and Sullivan, Software Reflexion Models: Bridging the Gap Between Source and High-Level Models (ACM SIGSOFT FSE 1995), compared an engineer's high-level model with source structure and produced convergence, divergence and absence relations. In the NetBSD example, an engineer obtained a useful overview of about 250,000 lines in hours. This is direct experience evidence for architecture drift, not a controlled accuracy study or prose-spec comparison.

Li, Liang, Soliman and Avgeriou, Understanding Software Architecture Erosion: A Systematic Mapping Study (Journal of Software: Evolution and Process, 2022), synthesized 73 studies and found erosion manifests as violations and structural problems affecting quality and evolution, while industrial empirical evidence remains limited. It supports recurring conformance analysis and explicitly limits confidence in universal remedies.

Delater and Paech, Tracing Requirements and Source Code during Software Development: An Empirical Study (ESEM 2013), evaluated semi-automatic links through work items in three undergraduate projects, reporting high precision and recall and positive usability. It supports maintaining traceability needed for drift checks, but the small student setting and semi-automatic workflow limit production generalization.
